metas.name: Bangladesh - Bollard
metas.note:
Bangladesh uses red-and-white concrete bollards throughout the whole country.

NOTE: They can also be found in a square form instead of a circular form.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Cambodia - Road 4 Bollard
metas.note:
Unique triangular bollards with red stripes can be found in three places in Cambodia, all located in the same area in the southwest:

  • On Road 4 between Angk Snuol and Preah Sihanouk. They are especially common in the section between Kirirom National Park and Preah Sihanouk.
  • One small off-road of Road 4, in Ream National Park near Preah Sihanouk.
  • In Preah Monivong National Park.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Road 48 Bollard
metas.note:
Black-and-white bollards in Cambodia are only found on Road 48, between Tatai and the intersection with Road 4.

NOTE: Make sure to check other clues before guessing, because this style of bollard is commonly found in Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bollards
metas.note:
Indonesia commonly uses these black-and-white square or circular bollards, as well as these yellow-and-black ones, which can also have a red reflector. Other designs can also be found.

NOTE: UK-style bollards are mostly found in Kalimantan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Japan - Akita Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Aomori Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Bollards
metas.note: In Japan, simple white bollards with circular or rectangular reflectors at the top are commonly used. However, sometimes these bollards are black, or have other extensions. They can also have the city or prefecture written on it in kanji.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/japan.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Yamaguchi Bollard
metas.note:
This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Okayama Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Striped Bollard
metas.note: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku Bollard
metas.note:
This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

Finally, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Japan - Toyama Bollard
metas.note:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.
metas.footer: ⓘ There may also be another type of bollard in this state

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.note: Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards. Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollard
metas.note: Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan.

metas.name: Malaysia - Bollards
metas.note:
Malaysian bollards will often have the colours black, white, grey and red. Here are three examples of typical Malaysian bollards.

NOTE: There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollard
metas.note: Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mongolia.

metas.name: Russia - Bollards
metas.note: Russia has three main types of bollards: a very thin type being attached to a stick, one with a black top section and a red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: South Korea - Bollard
metas.note: You will sometimes see these black and white wedge-shaped bollards. They have a round yellow reflector on the front, and a grey one on the back.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Bollard
metas.note: These short, wide stone bollards are unique to Sri Lanka. They have a tapered shape, with a black base and a white top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Bollards
metas.note:
Taiwan uses these bollards with either two or three circular reflectors on a black rectangle.

You can also find these lollipop looking reflectors on guardrails, similar to the designs found in Japan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/taiwan.

metas.name: Thailand - Bollards
metas.note:
The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has black-and-white and red-and-white stripes.

NOTE: In Southeast Asia, these bollards are also found in Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollard
metas.note: Turkish bollards are white and rectangular with a red reflector on the front, making them quite unique. Similar bollards exist in Romania but are very rare. Australian bollards typically have a reflector on the back and a slightly different design.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/turkey.

metas.name: Vietnam - Bollards
metas.note: In Vietnam, one type of bollard is primarily used. This bollard is white with a red tip and a yellow reflector on the front. However, a Spanish-type bollard made of stone can also rarely be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/vietnam for more clues.
